findings.claim: The PR fixes only the webhooks.ts PATCH /:id site, but the ticket identifies 15 adminConfig.ts catch blocks and the systemErrors.ts:196 instanceof check as the same pre-fail500 read hazard; none of those are changed, so the blast radius of the claimed fix is far narrower than the ticket's scope.
findings.evidence: ticket: "routes/adminConfig.ts: 15 catch blocks, at :189, :226, :289, :378, :433, :521, :702, :818, :933, :1226, :1389, :1567, :1658, :1695 and :1723. 13 of them open with `if (err?.message?.includes('does not exist') || err?.code === '42P01')` ... `:1567` reads `err?.message?.includes('does not exist')` with no code test." and "routes/systemErrors.ts:195-:199 ... `if (err instanceof z.ZodError) {` at `:196`"; diff only touches utils/pgErrors.ts and adds one test file.
findings.test_or_reason: The diff modifies only extractPgCode; no adminConfig.ts or systemErrors.ts file is touched, so the 15 adminConfig reads and the systemErrors instanceof check remain unguarded.

findings.claim: The PR's comment and test header claim the fix prevents a request from getting NO answer, but the fix only wraps extractPgCode in a try/catch; the same hazard remains in the 15 adminConfig.ts catch blocks and the systemErrors.ts instanceof check, so the claim that the class of pre-helper reads is fixed is false.
findings.evidence: test file line 1-2: "the catch of PATCH /api/webhooks/:id called `extractPgCode(err)` BEFORE it reached fail500. extractPgCode reads `code`, `meta.code` and `message` of the thrown value with no try of its own, so a revoked Proxy, or an object whose `code` getter throws, made the call throw inside the catch: the handler's promise rejected and the request got NO answer."
findings.test_or_reason: The ticket's item 2 lists 15 adminConfig blocks and the systemErrors.ts:196 instanceof check as the same shape; the PR does not touch those files, so the hazard persists there.

findings.claim: The new test B4 pins extractPgCode returning undefined for a throwing meta getter, but the implementation's try/catch wraps the entire readPgCode call, so the test passes even though the getter throw is caught; this is a valid pin but does not prove the route-level behavior for a meta getter (only B1/B2 cover route-level behavior, and only for code getter/revoked proxy).
findings.evidence: test line 98-104: "it('RED KS-1780 B4 extractPgCode of an object whose meta getter throws is undefined, not a throw', () => { const hostile = { get meta(): { code: string } { throw new Error('ks1780 meta getter'); } }; expect(pgCodeOrThrew(hostile)).toBeUndefined(); });"
findings.test_or_reason: The route-level tests B1/B2 use revokedProxy and throwingCodeGetter, but no route-level test uses a throwing meta getter; B4 only tests the helper directly.

findings.claim: The test file's header comment says "B1/B2 drive the real route over a loopback listener and read what the caller gets", but the route is mounted with a mocked auth middleware and a mocked db, so it is not the real production route; the claim of "real route" is overstated.
findings.evidence: test file line 15-17: "jest.mock('../middleware/auth', () => ({ authenticate: () => (_req: unknown, _res: unknown, next: () => void) => next(), }));" and line 7-13: "jest.mock('../db', () => ({ prisma: { $queryRaw: jest.fn(), $executeRaw: jest.fn(), $executeRawUnsafe: mockExecuteRawUnsafe } }));"
findings.test_or_reason: The route is exercised with mocked dependencies, so it is not the real production route; the comment's "real route" is misleading.

findings.claim: The ticket's acceptance criteria are not explicitly listed, but the PR addresses only the webhooks.ts site; the ticket's scope includes 15 adminConfig blocks and the systemErrors.ts instanceof check, so the acceptance of the ticket as a whole is not met.
findings.evidence: ticket: "The scan: in each route file that defines its own `fail500` ... `routes/adminConfig.ts`: 15 catch blocks ... `routes/systemErrors.ts:195`: item 1."
findings.test_or_reason: The diff does not touch adminConfig.ts or systemErrors.ts, so those sites remain unaddressed.

findings.claim: The PR's comment in pgErrors.ts says "A value that cannot be read has no code", which is a reasonable inference but not measured; the ticket itself says "Whether a thrown value of those shapes ... can reach any of these catches in practice" is not established.
findings.evidence: pgErrors.ts:53-54: "A revoked Proxy, or an object whose getter throws, makes one of them throw. The route catches that call this function BEFORE they reach fail500 ... A value that cannot be read has no code."
findings.test_or_reason: The ticket's "Not established" section explicitly says the reachability of such values in practice is unknown.
